newsitem.title: USA: Japanese climber rescued after fall in Yosemite.
newsitem.headline: Japanese climber rescued after fall in Yosemite.

text.p: A Japanese mountaineer was rescued by helicopter on Sunday after falling 30 feet (10 metres) during a solo climb in California's Yosemite National Park, park officials said.
Hideki Inaba, 33, fell on Friday while climbing the face of "El Capitan." He smashed his head into the granite rock face before coming to rest on a ledge, the officials said.
Members of his climbing party found his bloodstained helmet on Saturday and alerted park rangers, who flew to the top of El Capitan to rescue Inaba.
Rescuers hauled the injured man more than 600 feet (200 metres) up the rock face to the top of the cliff late on Saturday.

Because it was too dark to fly, Inaba and the 15-member rescue team spent Saturday night on the top of El Capitan. He was flown off the summit and taken to the park clinic for treatment on Sunday morning.
Inaba suffered a large cut behind his right ear and complained of back pain, but was reported in stable condition, said officials at Yosemite, 150 miles (240 km) southeast of San Francisco.
